newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat sees 150,000 new 1997 sales due scheme.
newsitem.headline: Fiat sees 150,000 new 1997 sales due scheme.

text.p: Italy's Fiat expects to sell some 150,000 extra new cars this year as a direct result of the government's plan to encourage motorists to trade in old cars for new, a senior Fiat Auto manager said.
Lelio Borla, head of sales for Milan, said in a television interview, "With these new measures we forecast total extra car sales of some 300,000, half of which will be Fiat group cars."
Fiat has a dominant position in the Italian market with a 44 percent share of domestic car sales. Total 1996 Italian new car registrations are expected to be around 1.7 million.

The government last week announced cash incentives to car owners to trade in scrap vehicles over 10 years old and buy new ones. Car makers will have to match each bonus on offer with a discount for the same amount.
The scheme, aimed to boost flagging domestic sales, took effect on Tuesday and will last until the end of September.
